content.title: Runoff changes after an ET refactor
content.observed_behavior: Total ET is nearly unchanged, but infiltration excess increases.
content.conditions: The ET calls were moved, cached soil deficit was retained, or units were converted at a different point.
content.candidate_causes: Changed process ordering; stale soil deficit; PET rate/depth mismatch; routing state reset.
content.reasoning: Routing cannot alter partitioned volume at its source. A stale or differently timed deficit directly changes partitioning capacity, so inspect ET ordering and deficit recomputation first.
content.recommended_action: Compare rainfall ET, retention ET, soil ET, deficit, infiltration, excess, and soil storage immediately before and after the refactor.

content.title: Mass balance closes, but the hydrograph is late
content.observed_behavior: Cumulative input and output close within tolerance, yet peak runoff arrives several timesteps too late.
content.conditions: Forcing conversion and total partitioned volumes match a reference run.
content.candidate_causes: GIUH ordinate shift; Nash K or N mismatch; routing state carried from another run; timestamp convention mismatch.
content.reasoning: Closed mass balance rules out lost or created water but not mistimed water. Because partitioned volumes agree, routing and clock alignment are more likely than infiltration parameters.
content.recommended_action: Compare direct, lateral, and groundwater components by timestep; inspect GIUH queue and Nash stores; then verify BMI current-time advancement.
